steps.text: We're down. Hard, but in one piece.
We came down on Mars, and we couldn't choose the spot.
Message received. Your signal takes minutes to reach me now, so I'll keep this short. Good luck.
Look at those rocks. This valley was carved by a giant flood, long ago.
And there, the Carl Sagan Memorial Station. Mars Pathfinder, landed on July 4, 1997.
It came down wrapped in giant airbags and bounced about 15 times, like a beach ball.
Then a rover the size of a microwave rolled down its ramp. Sojourner. Only 10.6 kilos.
If we copy those airbags, we can drop supplies anywhere on Earth without breaking them.

config.title: Time the airbags
config.prompt: Pathfinder is falling. Inflate the airbags at the right height above the ground.
config.hint: Too high and they slow you down too early. Too low and there is no time. Think of a football field.
config.learn: Pathfinder's computer inflated its airbags about 100 meters above Mars. It hit the ground at 14 m/s, bounced as high as 15 meters, and rolled to a stop about 1 km away. Its pictures of rounded pebbles showed that Mars once had running water.

steps.text: Over 16,000 pictures from the lander and 550 from Sojourner. Not bad for 1997, but we can do better with all these tech combined.
Spirit and Opportunity were twin rovers, landed on opposite sides of Mars. A long flight east.
There it is. Covered in dust. Opportunity landed in January 2004, three weeks after its twin, Spirit.
It was planned for 90 days. It drove for almost 15 years, 45 kilometers in total.
In June 2018 a dust storm covered the whole planet and blocked the sun. Its solar panels went dark.
It's real last signal was just data. People love to create drama from anything.
It was just a journalist who probably wanted his article to reach first page to earn more.
Fun fact from the old archives: only Perseverance ever drove farther on Mars, in October 2026.
Its panels still work. Let's wire them into our battery and bring them home.

config.title: Wire up Opportunity's panels
config.prompt: Connect each cable from the solar panel to the matching battery socket.
config.hint: Do the color you see best first. The letters on each plug help too.
config.learn: Spirit and Opportunity were robot geologists. By studying rocks, they confirmed that water stayed on the surface of ancient Mars for a long time. Wind sometimes blew the dust off Opportunity's solar panels, which helped it survive for years.

steps.text: Power is flowing. Fifteen years of dust storms, and these panels still work.
Last stop: Jezero Crater, an ancient lake bed.
A helicopter. On Mars. Ingenuity rode here under the belly of the Perseverance rover.
The air here is less than one percent as thick as on Earth. Flying should be almost impossible.
First flight: April 19, 2021. It was supposed to fly five times in 30 days. It flew 72 times in almost three years.
Only 1.8 kilos. A flying scout. With a few of these, we could search the whole Earth for survivors.
Then we take it home safely. Secure its mount.

config.title: Secure Ingenuity
config.prompt: Tighten the four bolts of the carrying mount in a criss-cross pattern.
config.hint: After a bolt, go to the one diagonally opposite.
config.learn: Ingenuity was the first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet. It flew for 128.8 minutes in total, covered 17 km and climbed as high as 24 meters. A solar panel charged its batteries, enough for about one 90-second flight per Martian day.

steps.text: Airbags, solar panels, a helicopter. Our new rover is starting to take shape.
Everyone aboard. We're going home.
